text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:
- Swiss Minister Flavio Cotti began his official visit to South America in Peru on Monday.
- Coop Group reported increased sales and its market share in 1996. It expects sales to grow by 2.5 percent more in the current year.
- Fromages Suisse SA, a cheese group consisting of 26 cheese trading firms, reportedly exported 33,116 tons of cheese and achieved sales of 318 million Swiss francs in 1996.

- Representatives from nearly 90 organisations protested against the use of genetically altered corn in food products in front of the Novartis headquarters in Basle. Further protests took place worldwide in over 100 cities.

- The Nordfinanz Bank, which was taken over by Union Bancaire Privee at the end of November 1995, posted a profit of 7.96 million Swiss francs for 1996. The number of employees was halved from 122 to 64.
- Peter Widmer will take over as new CEO of SLM (Schweizerische Lokomotiv und Maschinenfabrik AG), a subsidiary of the Sulzer Group.
- Coop, which radically changed its management structure in 1996, will make further cuts at the top.
- Roger de Weck, editor in chief of Zurich's daily "Tages-Anzeiger" newspaper announced his resignation, saying it is because of planned budget cuts. The paper has some 740,000 readers.
